subject: Pilot billing: microfloor alternatives & rounding clarification
messages:
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@arcadia.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify billing mechanics for our pilot

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we sign the pilot SOW we need to lock down a couple of billing mechanics so our finance team can model spend for Q4. Quick list of questions: 
- Do you round per-request to a minimum token quantum (e.g., 25 tokens) or bill strictly per-token?
- If we send many short messages (30–80 tokens), is there a way to aggregate/roll up to avoid inflated billing from a 25-token microfloor?
- How does long context (>=8k) affect metering — are there separate slabs or is billing purely based on generated + consumed tokens?
- Example: 150k calls/month, average prompt 45 tokens, average completion 55 tokens. Do you bill 150k * ceil((45+55)/quantum) or do you aggregate?

I've attached a small sample of their traffic to illustrate (arcadia_usage_sample.csv).

Can you send back a short worked example and any packaging options (commit tiers / microfloor concessions) you can offer for pilots?

Best,
Alex Jones
Head of Platform Engineering
Arcadia Systems
alex.jones@arcadia.com

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@arcadia.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-18T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify billing mechanics for our pilot

Alex —

Appreciate the concrete example, that helps. Short answer up front: we bill per-token but have two levers that often resolve the short-call inflation you described: (1) a micro-aggregation layer for pilot accounts (optional) that groups short calls within a configurable time window, and (2) an optional microfloor waiver for agreed commit levels. Below are the details and a worked example using your numbers.

Attachment: redwood_proposal_v1.pdf (proposal + example invoices)

Billing model (concise):
- Base unit: per-token (prompt + completion) measured by our tokenizer.
- Billing quantum: default 1 token (we do not round to 25 tokens by default). Historical microfloors you’ve seen are partner concessions.
- Session/window aggregation: for pilots we can enable a 60-second aggregation window that sums tokens for requests from the same session/client and bills the sum (reduces microfloor effects for chatty clients).
- Context slab handling: long-context processing is billed on total tokens used. There are no separate "slabs" for billing; slab terminology is for routing/throughput.

Worked example (your numbers):
- 150,000 calls/month
- Avg prompt 45 tokens, avg completion 55 tokens -> 100 tokens/call -> 15,000,000 tokens/month
- Default billing (per-token): 15,000,000 tokens billed. No rounding.
- If you previously saw a 25-token floor applied per-call, that could have increased costs to 150,000 * max(100,25) = still 15M (since 100 > 25). But in cases where avg < 25, a 25-token floor per-call would inflate billing.

Micro-aggregation effect (when average call < quantum):
- Example edge case: 150k calls with avg total 18 tokens/call -> raw tokens = 2.7M. If a 25-token per-call floor were applied you'd be billed 3.75M tokens. With a 60s aggregation window we bill close to the raw 2.7M (grouping many short calls).

Packaging/discounts we can offer for the pilot: 
- Pilot concession: enable aggregation + waive microfloor for first 3 months (no change to per-token price).
- Commit discount: 5% discount on unit price for a 6-month commit >= 12M tokens/month.
- True-up: monthly usage true-up; overages billed at committed unit price.

Next steps I suggest: (A) confirm whether Arcadia's short-call profile is common (your sample shows a mix), (B) if yes we'll enable aggregation for the pilot and include a temporary microfloor waiver in the SOW, (C) I'll loop in Kimberly from finance for final invoice wording if we move to a commit discount.

If you're OK I can push an updated SOW with the micro-aggregation clause and sample invoice that models both with/without the waiver.

Thanks —
Olga Petrov
Director, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@arcadia.com>

Olga —

Thanks, that explains a lot. A couple follow-ups from procurement: 
1) Aggregation window: 60s sounds reasonable, but what about cross-session aggregation (we use many short-lived clients)? Can you aggregate per-customer (API key) rather than per-session?
2) Commit math: we're not comfortable committing 12M/month up front. Would a stepped commit work (6M guaranteed month 1–3, step to 10M month 4–6) with pro-rated discount tiers?
3) Rounding: procurement insists invoices be reproducible. Can you provide the exact algorithm (pseudo-code) for how you sum tokens, round, and apply aggregation so our auditors can validate?

Sample observation from our data (attached): ~40% of calls are <20 tokens; ~30% are 20–60 tokens; remainder are longer. That means the microfloor waiver matters.

We'd like to avoid constant back-and-forth on wording. Can you produce a one-page "metering algorithm summary" we can attach to the SOW + a sample invoice that shows the stepped commit scenario?

Appreciate it,
Alex

Attachment: arcadia_usage_sample.csv

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Jones <alex.jones@arcadia.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot billing: microfloor alternatives & rounding clarification — recommendation and wording for SOW

Kimberly / Sergio —

Forwarding Arcadia's follow-up. Key asks: (1) per-customer aggregation option (not just session), (2) stepped commit flexibility, (3) reproducible metering pseudo-code for auditors.

My recommended concession:
- Enable per-API-key aggregation window (60s by default, configurable) for the pilot only.
- Include a 3-month pilot microfloor waiver in the SOW (waive any partner-specific per-call microfloor) to be effective for months 1–3.
- Offer stepped commit proposal: 6M tokens/month (months 1–3) -> 10M tokens/month (months 4–6) with tiered discounts (3% for 6M floor, 5% once >=10M). True-up monthly.
- Provide a metering appendix (one-page) with deterministic steps and a sample invoice. I drafted the pseudo-code below as a starting point for legal/finance: 

Pseudo-code (metering appendix, short):
1) For each API key, collect all requests in the billing period.
2) For each request: tokens = tokenizer.count(prompt) + tokenizer.count(completion).
3) If aggregation_enabled: group requests by API key into fixed windows (window_size_seconds). For each window, window_tokens = sum(tokens in window).
4) Monthly_total_tokens = sum(window_tokens for all windows).
5) Apply committed_allowance (if any): billed_tokens = max(Monthly_total_tokens, committed_allowance).
6) Apply tiered_discount based on committed_allowance thresholds.
7) Invoice = billed_tokens * unit_price * (1 - discount).

Notes: the microfloor waiver is implemented by skipping any partner-specific per-request minimum in step 2 when aggregation_enabled is true. This keeps the actual per-token accounting deterministic and reproducible.

I attached a short draft metering appendix and a sample invoice spreadsheet to the Drive link above; want Kimberly to confirm legal-friendly wording (and whether we need any additional audit logs wording). Sergio, please confirm ops can enable per-API-key aggregation for the pilot.

If all good I'll update the SOW and send Arcadia the one-pager + sample invoice.

Thanks,
Olga
